text.p1-meaning-open-phone:
What these results mean, and what they cannot tell you

WHAT THE FOUR OUTCOMES MEAN

Meets published requirements: every recorded rule is met — shown as Quota 2 only where you are below the floor for the main route, so only that route is open.
Possible with action: every gap has a named step you can finish for this intake — one test, or supplementary courses no more than the university is recorded as allowing after your results, and at most two (our limit).
Does not currently meet: a gap with no recorded step, or steps that do not fit this intake.
Needs review: missing or unverified data, a permission nobody has recorded, or a rule a person must judge.

WHAT THIS CANNOT TELL YOU

This checks published requirements. It does not predict whether you will be offered a place — for programmes with restricted admission, meeting the requirements is where the competition starts, not where it ends. Past cut-offs are shown as context and are never used as a rule.
text.p1-how-open-phone:
How to close a gap
At AU (3 results): AU accepts supplementary courses, and counts College Board AP and British A-level courses as A level. Pass it by 5 July, or after 5 July as conditional admission with documentation by 5 September (at most two after 5 July).
At SDU (12 results): SDU accepts supplementary courses. An EU/EEA applicant who has not finished by 5 July is offered a place conditional on passing by 31 August.
Where the institution names no route of its own (12 results): Take the level as a Danish supplementary course (gymnasial supplering) passed by 5 July; where the programme accepts it, one subject can instead be taken as summer supplementation after 5 July, with your place conditional on passing it before the programme starts.
